provenance_card: The kinds of work shown come from Schoenfeld’s categories of mathematical problem solving, as set out by Li et al. (2025).

Those definitions were written for other settings: a reasoning model’s written solutions, and video of university students solving geometry problems. Using them on tutoring turns goes beyond the settings where those definitions were tested.
The episodes in this report were proposed by a language model.

These sessions were marked by the model and, separately, by an annotator generated for this demo. The two lined up closely enough for this view to be shown. Lining up is not evidence that either marking is right.
Nobody has established how reliably these labels can be applied. This report describes what happened in the sessions and claims nothing beyond that.

The episode detail is shown only when the model’s marking and a second, separate marking of the same sessions agree at 0.61 or above on Cohen’s kappa, a measure of how closely two markings agree beyond chance.
The definitions were developed on mathematics and are used here on mathematics only.
